evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: We value robust data design, but we operate in a fast-paced business. Success means developing the pragmatism to know when a scalable, long-term model is required, and when an iterative solution is the right call.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD explicitly balances rigour signals (automated testing, documentation, canonical source of truth) with explicit velocity language ('fast-paced business', iterative solutions valued over perfect architecture), giving mixed.
evidence.domain_risk: This role offers a rare opportunity to structure complex financial domains - from client portfolios and fund transactions to multi-currency valuations across two markets.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Endowus is a licensed wealth manager (MAS, SFC) handling client portfolios and fund transactions, meeting the default-high fintech/regulated-finance bar for domain risk.
evidence.data_team_maturity: We are hiring our first Analytics Engineer to build the data models and metric definitions that power analytics across Endowus.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The JD explicitly states this is the company's first Analytics Engineer hire with no mature standards or stack yet ('Analytics engineering is a growing discipline here'), a clear early-stage signal.
evidence.jd_authorship: Implement automated testing, freshness monitoring, and dbt documentation so model changes are traceable, tested, and reliable.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities are precise about tools (dbt, semantic layer), concrete tasks, and even an unusually candid 'Why Not Endowus' section describing real day-to-day tradeoffs, strongly indicating hiring-manager authorship.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You will design models that enable core teams including Product, Marketing, and Operations to get to answers faster.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The JD names Product, Marketing, and Operations as roughly equally weighted stakeholder groups alongside internal data-platform work, giving mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: taking full ownership of our semantic layer and analytics architecture, bridging into data engineering, or driving technical direction as the team expands
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The JD combines strategic growth language (own the semantic layer, drive technical direction) with junior-appropriate execution framing (1-3 years experience, defined must-haves for a first hire), giving mixed.
evidence.ai_role: You actively use AI tools to accelerate your work, driven by a genuine curiosity about our data and business.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is explicitly expected to use AI tools to accelerate their own work ('AI-native curiosity'), matching ai_user; the JD's mention of 'AI-assisted workflows' the candidate's models must support is a secondary, weaker signal.
evidence.testing_framing: Implement automated testing, freshness monitoring, and dbt documentation so model changes are traceable, tested, and reliable.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and monitoring are listed as an owned responsibility ('Make it trustworthy') with action verbs, not just a tool mention.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: the automated tests that keep them reliable, and the metric definitions feeding our semantic layer and BI tools
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust, reliability, and a 'canonical source of truth' for financial metrics are recurring themes throughout responsibilities, reflecting a high loss-aversion framing centered on data trustworthiness in a regulated financial context.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: We are hiring our first Analytics Engineer to build the data models and metric definitions that power analytics across Endowus.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The JD explicitly frames this as the first analytics engineering hire building conventions and patterns from the ground up, a clear greenfield signal.
evidence.loss_aversion: the automated tests that keep them reliable, and the metric definitions feeding our semantic layer and BI tools — reliability and a single source of truth for financial metrics is a recurring, dominant theme given the regulated wealth-management context.

responsibilities: Model the data. Build and maintain dbt models end-to-end, collaborating with Data Engineering and software engineers to transform source data into clean, intuitive models for business teams.
Make it trustworthy. Implement automated testing, freshness monitoring, and dbt documentation so model changes are traceable, tested, and reliable.
Govern the metrics. Partner with business stakeholders and analysts to standardise core metric definitions, establishing a canonical source of truth for key business numbers.
Enable self-serve. Support our transition to a dbt-native BI layer, designing data models and semantic definitions that make independent querying intuitive for cross-functional teams.
